Name: Pathfinder Valley
Author: war77
Description:
[center]
[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/50678/50678-1786647498-1483908897.png[/img]

[size=6][b][color=#E6B94E]PATHFINDER VALLEY[/color][/b][/size]

[size=4][i]Every road begins with a few footsteps.[/i][/size]
[/center]

[quote]
The people of Stardew Valley have spent years walking the same roads—but now, your footsteps can create roads of their own.[/quote]
[b]Pathfinder Valley[/b] introduces a dynamic trail system inspired by the natural “desire paths” that appear wherever people repeatedly walk.

As you travel through outdoor areas, the ground remembers your movements. Frequently traveled routes gradually change from flattened grass into dirt, gravel, rough stone, and eventually cobblestone.

Your farm and the surrounding valley will slowly develop a network of paths based entirely on the routes you actually use!

[center]
[size=5][b][color=#7DA65A]HOW IT WORKS[/color][/b][/size]
[/center]

Every outdoor tile records how many times you walk onto it during the current day.

[list]
[*][b]Walk across a tile once:[/b] No change.[/*]
[*][b]Walk across a tile two or more times:[/b] The tile gains one wear point at the end of the day.[/*]
[*][b]Continue crossing it afterward:[/b] No additional wear is added that day.[/*]
[/list]
A tile can gain a maximum of [b]one wear point per day[/b], whether you cross it twice or fifty times.

This allows paths to emerge naturally over several days without suddenly changing from grass to stone after one busy afternoon.
[center]
[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/50678/50678-1786647491-50866861.png[/img][/center]
[center]
[size=5][b][color=#B9854B]THE PATH PROGRESSION[/color][/b][/size]
[/center]

As a natural tile gains wear, its appearance gradually changes through seven stages:

[list=1]
[*][b]Flattened grass[/b][/*]
[*][b]Thinning grass[/b][/*]
[*][b]Exposed dirt[/b][/*]
[*][b]Packed dirt[/b][/*]
[*][b]Gravel[/b][/*]
[*][b]Rough embedded stones[/b][/*]
[*][b]Established cobblestone[/b][/*]
[/list]
The routes you use most often will become the most developed, while occasional shortcuts may remain as faint grass or dirt trails.

[center]
[size=5][b][color=#7DA65A]NATURE RECLAIMS UNUSED PATHS[/color][/b][/size]
[/center]

Trails do not remain forever if you stop using them.

If you do not cross a worn tile during an entire day, it [b]loses one wear point[/b]. An abandoned cobblestone route will gradually return through rough stone, gravel, dirt, and flattened grass before finally blending back into the natural landscape.

[list]
[*][b]No crossings that day:[/b] The tile loses one wear point.[/*]
[*][b]One crossing that day:[/b] The tile remains unchanged.[/*]
[*][b]Two or more crossings that day:[/b] The tile gains one wear point.[/*]
[/list]
Walking across a tile exactly once therefore pauses its recovery without making the path more developed.

[center]
[size=5][b][color=#9DA8B3]STONE FLOORING IS PROTECTED[/color][/b][/size]
[/center]

Any stone or masonry flooring that is already present will remain untouched.

This includes:

[list]
[*]Cobblestone flooring[/*]
[*]Stone flooring[/*]
[*]Gravel flooring[/*]
[*]Brick flooring[/*]
[*]Crystal flooring[/*]
[*]Stepping-stone paths[/*]
[*]Other non-wood flooring[/*]
[/list]
Pathfinder Valley will never wear down or replace these surfaces.

Manually placed flooring also takes visual priority over any natural trail progress saved underneath it.

[center]
[size=5][b][color=#B8793E]WOODEN FLOORS CAN WEAR OUT[/color][/b][/size]
[/center]

Wooden flooring is less durable than stone, but it takes time to deteriorate.

A wooden floor can gain no more than [b]one damage point per day[/b]. It must receive three qualifying daily damage points before its appearance changes.

[list]
[*][b]3 damage points:[/b] The boards appear worn.[/*]
[*][b]6 damage points:[/b] The boards appear cracked and badly damaged.[/*]
[*][b]9 damage points:[/b] The wooden flooring finally breaks away.[/*]
[/list]
Unused wooden flooring recovers [b]one damage point per day[/b], giving lightly traveled boards time to recover before permanent damage occurs.

Wood, weathered-wood, and boardwalk-style flooring are included in this system.

[center]
[size=5][b][color=#D3A557]ORGANIC PATHS—NOT INVENTORY FLOORING[/color][/b][/size]
[/center]

The trails created by Pathfinder Valley are visual terrain surfaces rather than ordinary flooring items.

This means naturally created paths:

[list]
[*]Do not fill your inventory with flooring.[/*]
[*]Do not interfere with deliberately placed stone paths.[/*]
[*]Develop and recover gradually.[/*]
[*]Remain tied to the tiles where they formed.[/*]
[*]Are saved with your current farm.[/*]
[/list]
[center]
[size=5][b][color=#75A7C8]CONFIGURATION[/color][/b][/size]
[/center]

The included configuration file allows you to adjust:

[list]
[*]The number of crossings required to qualify for daily wear[/*]
[*]The maximum natural trail stage[/*]
[*]Whether abandoned trails decay[/*]
[*]The damage points required for each wooden-floor stage[/*]
[*]The number of wooden-floor stages before removal[/*]
[*]Whether the system works everywhere outdoors or only on the farm[/*]
[/list]
[center]
[size=5][b][color=#C7A9E8]REQUIREMENTS[/color][/b][/size]
[/center]

[list]
[*][b]Stardew Valley 1.6[/b][/*]
[*][b]SMAPI 4.0 or newer[/b][/*]
[/list]
No additional framework mods are required.

[center]
[size=5][b][color=#E6B94E]INSTALLATION[/color][/b][/size]
[/center]

[list=1]
[*]Install SMAPI.[/*]
[*]Download and extract Pathfinder Valley.[/*]
[*]Place the [b]PathfinderValley[/b] folder inside your [b]Stardew Valley/Mods[/b] folder.[/*]
[*]Launch Stardew Valley through SMAPI.[/*]
[*]Start walking—and watch the valley remember where you have been.[/*]
[/list]
[center]
[size=5][b][color=#7DA65A]LET YOUR FARM TELL ITS STORY[/color][/b][/size]
[/center]

Pathfinder Valley transforms your everyday movement into part of the landscape.

The shortcut you take to your crops, the route you follow into town, and the trail leading to your favorite fishing spot can all become visible pieces of your farm’s history.

[center]
[size=4][b][i]Every road begins with a few footsteps.[/i][/b][/size]
[/center]
